asks.source_span: This document or reference to other relevant guidance documents should provide additional details on the types of interactions that sponsors should expect (e.g. meeting/written feedback) and timelines for such interactions for submissions seeking Agency advice on the use of RWD.

As such, this guidance document should make clear that this is a dynamic topic and highlight the Agency’s flexibility and receptivity in engaging with Sponsor to advise on and explore other concerns, approaches, and considerations specific to individual drug development programs.

Regeneron requests that in some circumstances the draft guidance also consider situations when the sponsor does not directly control the procedures leading to the creation of the final study-specific dataset. The guideline should provide recommendations for best practices when information regarding data accrual, curation, and transformation is not available.

The Agency could also include language in this guidance to encourage data owners/processors to share this information with Sponsors and the Agency so it can be utilized as a reference to the use of RWD and Agency reviews.
Regeneron recommends that the Agency add OMOP and FHIR as other common data standards to use for RWD mapping in this section.
As stated in our prior comments 4 , we respectfully request that FDA recommend processes by which an RWD/E organization could request a meeting with the

it would be beneficial to stakeholders for the Agency to acknowledge in the Final Guidance that there may be cases where sufficient mapping may not be possible and to provide guidance on what FDA’s approach would be under such circumstances.

we recommend that FDA consider accelerating the expansion of the Data Standards Catalog to include data formats that are more amenable to using RWD sources, including standards that address cases when multiple data sources are linked.
we encourage FDA to consider expedited steps that address these issues and consider sharing a more comprehensive strategy for accommodating the submission of studies using RWD.
Flatiron would appreciate clarity on whether FDA expects these same compliance checks to be conducted for regulatory submissions containing RWD/E,
encourages the Agency to consider working with RWD/E organizations and sponsors to develop compliance check tools that are tailored to these datasets in order to streamline submissions.
Lastly, in cases where there are compliance rule discrepancies, Flatiron requests clarity on how to handle these issues when they arise and recommends FDA provide additional guidance on this topic.

We encourage the FDA to provide alternative approaches of data standardization according to different sources of RWD as one standard format (e.g., CDISC standards) under the Data Standards Catalog may risk losing key clinical specificity and benefit added from using RWD (e.g., unstructured text).
It would be helpful if the FDA would outline specific procedures about when to approach the agency using offline correspondence and in-person consultations/meetings.
Any additional resources such as case studies, examples, white papers, will be beneficial in providing further applicability of this guidance document.
(Line 95-103) We ask FDA to provide further instructions on how to document and detail an adequate process to ensure that submitted documents meet FDA standards.
We also ask for further clarification on how “confidence in data” would be defined and/or demonstrated.
we recommend that FDA facilitate workshops with a broad audience that can help provide input and collaboratively craft the next Catalog.
We also suggest providing specific guidance on applying data standards to linked data from multiple RWD sources.
We recommend that FDA accept the use of other programming languages (e.g., R, Python), including some of their packages or modules, if they adhere to the appropriate process and methodology.
We ask for further guidance on how to validate information related to those packages or modules outside of the standard format.

(Line 137-145) It would be helpful if FDA would refer therapeutic area-specific study data submission guidelines or at least outline that they exist and that sponsors should make sure to consider whether they apply to their submissions.

We also ask for clarification on the use of Common Data Models (CDMs) where some variables of multiple CDMs are used and/or additional variables may need to be created outside those CDMs or even outside of the CDISC terminology.
